title: The third answer: mind is Brahman
theme: The formula repeats with mind: beings are born of mind, live by it and go into it. Bhṛgu returns once more, and is sent back to austerity.

sandhi.type: visarga before a voiced consonant; guṇa
sandhi.rule: manaḥ before the voiced b: P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) and P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः); brahma + iti → brahmeti by P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः).

sandhi.type: visarga before a voiced consonant; yaṇ
sandhi.rule: manasaḥ before h: P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) and P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः). hi + eva → hyeva, P. 6.1.77 (इको यणचि).
u before a dissimilar vowel becomes v: P. 6.1.77 (इको यणचि).
prayanti + abhi-: P. 6.1.77 (इको यणचि). abhisaṃviśanti + iti → -īti: P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः).
A final t becomes d before a voiced consonant: P. 8.2.39 (झलां जशोऽन्ते).
punaḥ ends in an original r, which reappears before a vowel: punar eva.

sandhi.type: visarga before a voiced consonant; guṇa
sandhi.rule: bhagavaḥ before the voiced b: the visarga becomes u, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च), and a + u gives o, P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः). brahma + iti → brahmeti, also by P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः).
As bhagavo brahmeti: P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) and P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः).

sandhi.type: saḥ before a consonant; aḥ before a
sandhi.rule: saḥ loses its ending before a consonant, P. 6.1.132 (एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि). tapaḥ before a: the visarga becomes u, P. 6.1.113 (अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते), a + u → o, and the following a is absorbed, P. 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्तादति), written with avagraha.
The visarga becomes s before t: P. 8.3.34 (विसर्जनीयस्य सः).

morphology.note: Imperfect of vi-√jñā (ninth class, stem jānā-), with the augment a after the preverb: vi + a-jānāt → vyajānāt. It supplies the main verb for the absolutive taptvā that ended the previous anuvāka.
Ablative of manas (s-stem); before h its visarga becomes o (manaso hy eva). Here hi stands without the preceding t-stop that produced ddh in the other anuvākas.

translation.literal: [Having practised austerity,] he understood: ‘Mind is Brahman.’ For from mind, indeed, surely, these beings are born; by mind, born, they live; into mind they go forth [and] enter. Having understood that, he approached [his] father Varuṇa once more: ‘Teach [me] Brahman, venerable one.’ He said to him: ‘By austerity seek to know Brahman. Austerity is Brahman.’ He practised austerity. Having practised austerity —
translation.readable: Having practised austerity, he understood that mind is Brahman: for it is from mind that these beings are born, by mind that they live once born, and into mind that they pass and merge at the end. Having understood this, he went to his father Varuṇa again and said, ‘Sir, teach me Brahman.’ Varuṇa told him: ‘Seek to know Brahman by austerity. Austerity is Brahman.’ He practised austerity, and when he had practised it —

syntax: The same frame as 3.2 and 3.3, with the four case forms of manas. The base file drops a letter in upasasāra here (corrected).

ambiguities.topic: How are beings born of mind?
ambiguities.note: Kūranārāyaṇa: all knowing, acting and ceasing depend on mind, and when mind departs all is lost («मन आयत्तत्वाच्च सर्वबोद्धप्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तीनाम्»; «मनोविगमे सर्वस्य विनाशाच्च»); he also cites the Gītā, where mind is one of the eight parts of nature. Rāmānanda, by contrast, explains Bhṛgu’s dissatisfaction: the Chāndogya says mind is made of food («अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः»), so mind too is produced.

metre.name: prose
metre.note: Prose (brāhmaṇa style) in short clauses, divided at the daṇḍas.

beginner: The third time round, Bhṛgu decides that mind is Brahman. This goes deeper than food and breath: everything we know and do passes through the mind, and when the mind goes, our whole world goes with it. It looks like the source, support and end of everything we experience. Yet once again Bhṛgu returns to his father unsatisfied, and once again the answer is the same: practise austerity. One commentator explains why the mind still falls short: another Upaniṣad says the mind is made from food, so it too depends on something else. The search continues inward.
analogy: A screen shows everything we watch, but the screen is not where the pictures come from.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Bhṛgu concludes that mind is Brahman, because beings are born of mind, live by it and go into it. He returns, asks again, and is again told to seek Brahman by austerity.

commentary.q: In what sense do beings come from mind?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Kūranārāyaṇa: mind governs all knowing, acting and ceasing («मन आयत्तत्वाच्च सर्वबोद्धप्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तीनाम्»), and when it departs everything perishes for the person («मनोविगमे सर्वस्य विनाशाच्च»); he cites the Gītā, which counts mind among the eight parts of nature, to show that mind is a principle of the world.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Rāmānanda: another scripture says mind is made of food («अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः»), so mind is a product, subject to coming and going, and cannot be Brahman («मनसः अन्नविकारत्वावगमात्»).

commentary.q: What do the forms tell us?
commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: manas is an s-stem: ablative manasaḥ, instrumental manasā, accusative manaḥ. Before hi the ablative becomes manaso, so this anuvāka has manaso hy eva where the others have -ād dhy eva. The base file drops the p of upasasāra here, restored from the other anuvākas and the witnesses (corrections.json).

advaita.text: No comment of Śaṅkara’s own on this anuvāka (the rest is plain, «ऋज्वन्यत्»). Mind, like food and breath, shows only part of the mark; the series moves inward to bliss («शनैः शनैः अन्तरनुप्रविश्य अन्तरतममानन्दं ब्रह्म विज्ञातवान्»).

visistadvaita.text: Mind truly governs the whole of a creature’s activity («मनोविगमे सर्वस्य विनाशाच्च»), but it is a product of food, as the Chāndogya says («अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः»), and so it is not the final cause.

dvaita.text: Viṣṇu is called ‘mind’ because he is the thinker («मनो मन्तृत्वतस्तथा»); this is the next of his forms that Bhṛgu came to know.

schools.disagreement: As in 3.2–3.3. Madhva’s reading differs in kind: ‘mind’ names the Lord as thinker, not the human faculty.

parallels.note: The self made of mind lies within the self made of breath in the Brahmānandavallī; the third step of Bhṛgu’s search is the same.
Rāmānanda cites the Chāndogya’s teaching that mind is made of food to explain why Bhṛgu was not satisfied with mind.

contemporary.text: Much of modern life treats attention as the most valuable thing there is, and it is easy to conclude that whatever holds the mind is what matters most. The passage grants the mind its power and still asks what lies beneath it. This is a modern reflection on the passage, not part of its traditional meaning.

reflect.beginner: How much of your day is shaped by what your mind is busy with?
reflect.deeper: If the mind depends on the body, as the Chāndogya says, can the mind be the source of everything?
reflect.practice: For a minute, watch thoughts arise and pass without following them, and notice that you can notice them.

references.text: The base file reads पितरमुससार, dropping the p; corrected to पितरमुपससार from every other anuvāka, S and Madhva’s text (corrections.json).
Gopālānanda comments only «स्पष्टोऽर्थः» (‘the sense is clear’).
